title: Phased Cutover PRD for Hosted Multi‑Modal Endpoints — Traffic Slicing & Eval‑Gated Launch Playbook
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Purpose: Define an executable PRD + launch playbook for rolling out a unified hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) using phased traffic cutover slices gated by automated evaluation and operational signals. This doc balances product acceptance requirements, risk controls, and runbook steps to minimize customer-facing regressions while enabling incremental capacity expansion.

Background: Recent model surface unification work touches contracts and behaviour across four endpoint types. We must ensure behavior parity, determinism bounds, latency SLOs, and cost targets while enabling a progressive rollout that can be paused/rolled-back automatically. This ticket codifies acceptance criteria, test harnesses, monitoring signals, and launch slices for safe production activation.
requirements: Behavioral: No more than 1.5% regression in key behavior probes vs baseline across generation and rerank on the primary eval suite (see eval-run-2026-02 link).
Determinism: Seeded generation reproducibility within defined variance band for same-model same-config requests (delta < 0.2 BLEU-like token-level metric for deterministic lanes).
Latency: 95th percentile tail latency <= 450ms for completions (<= 600ms for chat multi-turn median context), measured under representative QPS load.
Throughput & Cost: Sustained QPS per lane must meet cost-per-token budget targets; autoscaling triggers defined to limit unit cost blowouts (>25% above baseline triggers automated traffic reduction).
Compatibility: Embeddings and rerank responses must preserve previous similarity ordering on canonical test cases (top-5 stable ordering), with noted exceptions documented in migration-notes-2026-02.
API Contract: Backwards-compatible request/response shapes. New optional fields are opt-in and have clear fail-safe defaults.
Operational: Per-route SLOs surfaced in Console, with canary dashboards and alerting (on-call playbooks attached).
Security & Compliance: KMS-encrypted payload logging for PII-sensitive tenants; audit logs enabled for Private/Dedicated customers before traffic increases beyond slice 2.
non_goals: Model architecture changes or new model onboarding (this PRD assumes previously validated model variants).
Comprehensive cost optimization beyond configured burst/autoscaling policies — further Optimize work will follow.
Implementing tenant-level advanced RBAC flows (out of scope for initial phased rollout).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Eval gating — daily automated eval job (end-to-end) passes with regression <1.5% on composite behavioral score for the release candidate across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank.
A2: Latency & throughput — synthetic load test with representative traffic shape shows 95p latency within SLO and autoscaler maintains target concurrency for 30m soak without errors.
A3: Observability — per-route telemetry (token counts, cost estimate, KV cache hit rate, batch sizes) visible in Console; at least 3 dashboards created and shared with SRE/PM/Eng reviewers.
A4: Safety & Contract — optional fields backward-compatibility tests pass; clients without new fields behave unchanged on 500 canonical regression cases.
A5: Canary stage metrics — no critical alerts and no customer-impacting errors during a 48-hour canary window at slice 1 (<=1k unique users equivalent).
A6: Rollback hooks — automated policy triggers to reduce traffic or switch to fallback model variant on metric breach implemented and exercised in staging.
rollout_steps: Slice 0 (internal): Feature flagged for internal-only traffic. Duration: 72h soak. Objectives: exercise code paths, validate logs, smoke detect edge errors.
Slice 1 (partner beta): 0.1% production traffic routed to new surface for selected low-risk tenants. Duration: 48h. Gate: A1-5 pass and no Sev1 incidents.
Slice 2 (gradual ramp): 2% traffic, broader tenant set, enable KMS and audit logging for tenants opted into Private/Dedicated. Duration: 72h. Gate: stable latency and cost within 15% of baseline.

Slice 3 (regional ramp): 10% traffic per-region, enable autoscaler burst policies, monitor cross-region fallbacks. Duration: rolling 7 days. Gate: regional SLOs stable, no increase in customer complaints.
Slice 4 (general availability): Flip default routing; continue monitoring for 30 days with weekly quality regressions review.
rollback_triggers: Severity 1 customer-impacting errors (any production 500s correlated with the new surface).
Behavioral regression breaches: composite eval score delta > 1.5% sustained for two consecutive daily runs.
Latency SLO breach: 95p latency > 2x SLO for 30 minutes under normal traffic.
Cost blowout: unit token cost > 25% of baseline for sustained 1 hour despite autoscaler adjustments.
Unexpected spike in cache-miss ratio causing increased op load (KV hit rate < 40% and growing).
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-endpoint summary (QPS, 95/99 latencies, errors), behavioral eval tracker, cost-per-token estimator.
Alerts: P95 latency >= SLO (severity P1), error rate spike (+5x baseline) (severity P0), eval regression alarms (P1).
Tracing: end-to-end request traces anchored to model variant and route; sampling for multi-turn chat.
Logs: structured request/response metadata with redaction rules; sample size of payload captures configurable via Console.
test_plan: Unit & integration: contract tests for request/response envelopes; fuzzing for optional fields and backwards compatibility.
Synthetic load tests: shape-based traffic (burst, steady, tail-heavy) with KV cache priming scenarios.

Behavioral eval suite: 12k prompt-probe set covering generation, multi-turn chat, embeddings similarity checks, and rerank precision cases. Baseline snapshots stored in drive: drive.redwood/evals/baseline-2026-02.
Chaos checks: simulated spindle/region degradation to validate graded fallback to compatible model variants.
Canary verification: automated smoke runbook that validates smoke endpoints, billing signals, and sample qualitative review from PM/Design.
dependencies: ENG-21234: Autoscaler tuning for per-route concurrency limits (blocking for Slice 2+).
ENG-21999: KV cache priming API and fast invalidation endpoints.
ENG-22001: Rollout flag infra and automated rollback orchestration.
SEC-412: KMS enablement and tenant encryption gating for Private customers.
DOCS-81: Customer-facing migration notes and API change log.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: We accept a slightly relaxed latency SLO for chat multi-turn lanes during early slices to reduce headroom pressure and focus on behavioral stability. This is documented in slice gating criteria.

Decision: Use model-variant fallbacks for severe tail latency cases rather than synchronous degradation to shorter contexts to preserve user experience. Team will track quality impact in rerank probes.
Open question: Whether to expose a new client opt-in header for experimental deterministic lane. Engineering prefers flag-first rollout; PM to confirm API approach by 2026-03-05.
